subject: Cat colony help
content:
Good morning,

My name is Jake and I'm reaching out because my in-laws live in the country and have created an impromptu cat colony by feeding the cats on their farm.

They've done this for years without issue, the cats would generally leave after a month or two; the population never increased to more than 2-3 at most. However due to the amount of development around Hunt County in the last year, all of the surrounding grasslands that the cats used to live in are now subdivisions. As a result, the cats are not leaving and we need to start spaying/neutering them to control the population. At the moment, there are currently about 10-15 cats and at least one is pregnant.

The colony address is: 4785 CR 2664, Royse City TX 75189

Can you point us in the direction of resources to trap the cats and then spay/neuter them? We understand some costs may be incurred but my in laws can not afford to pay a vet the retail price out of pocket for a dozen cats. They are happy to continue feeding the cat colony, but need help getting the population under control without paying thousands of dollars in vet costs.

Any help would be greatly appreciated. Please email me here or call/text me at 469-224-3184.

Thanks,

Sent with[Proton Mail](https://proton.me/mail/home)secure email.

subject: feral natured young male orange young cat
content:
Hi !! today is Tuesday,  April 29th, 2025, My husband and I need help desperately. We love, love cats, we have 2  beautiful indoor cats. Anyway, in our yard out of nowhere, this beautiful,  healthy, lovable, affectionate kitty comes on our front porch, he is very kind, sweet, very clean, this kitty loves car rides and loves hugs and loves to be held. We can not afford another kitty. We have our cats on great health plans,  spade and neutered, spoiled rotten in a good way. They love walks, they love their play tent outside. This feral TNR kitty will not let our kitty's in their tent, he thinks it's his house, and yard. My husband and I took him to Grand Prairie Paws Adoption Center in Grand Prairie,  they would not even check him for a chip. !!! When this kitty was 1st trapped, someone took him to Grand Prairie Paws Adoption Center,  they TNR, this kitty, it's obviously this kitty was an inside cat, someone took him in, than dumped him !!! He knows the word No, he has the lightest hazel/ light green eyes. Many of our friends have 2 or more cats. This sweet one just wants a forever home, to be loved, rubbed, patted, cared for. We are 74 & 76, we can take care of our cats very well, we just can not afford this precious kitty. In the car, he just lays there, he loves car rides!  Can you help us please? John and Suzanne Mason of Grand Prairie,  Tx, 75052, cell # 972-891-5289,  E-Mail: suzanne.mason69@yahoo.com,  thank you,so much if you can help. Thank you
